scope: Corollary 2.7 (Pointwise angular exclusion) of the manuscript “Elliptic capacity propagation and Fourier restriction to the sphere” (preprints/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026/Elliptic-capacity-propagation-and-Fourier-restriction-to-the-sphere-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 077 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 669efdbef9150144), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 16. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let H be the family in Corollary 2.6. Suppose a large sublaw ν ≤ µ carries assigned boxes C(z) ∈ H, with z ∈ C(z). Assume the cap is also available at all enlarged widths used below. After removing o(ν(whole space)) mass, the following implication holds pointwise: z ∈ Md D, D ∈ H =⇒ ∠(C(z), D) ≤ w L MCκ(e+d)+o(1) . Here D is in the particle’s time bin, and dilation acts on each spatial rectangle about its own center. One retained set works simultaneously for the dyadic dilations in any fixed power range d ≥ 0.
